solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Degradation of middle, now vulgar

indicators.note: degradation breaks something down, so the following words are reduced to rubble and rebuilt in another order

blocks.note: the two words taken as written supply the letters

explanation.surface: A complaint that the middle classes are now being coarsened and debased.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with base, crude tastes and coarse thoughts is called vulgar, the same sense in a hyphenated adjective.

clue.text: Wish magistrate to restrict dubious pronouncement for contest

indicators.note: restricting something hems it in, so the magistrate's letters close around the doubtful sound

blocks.note: to long for something is to wish for it
JP is a Justice of the Peace, a lay magistrate in Britain
um is the hesitant noise of someone unsure

explanation.surface: Someone hopes a magistrate will curb a questionable ruling about a competition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a track-and-field athletics event in which competitors leap for distance, so it is one example of a sporting competition.

clue.text: Lived honestly, less content and not at full strength

indicators.note: without its content a word keeps only its shell, the first and final letters

blocks.note: was means existed, lived
the outside letters of honestly

explanation.surface: Someone who lived an honest life, was less satisfied and felt weakened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' reads as happy, but here it means what is inside a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Washy describes a drink or colour that is watery and diluted, therefore weak and lacking strength.

clue.text: The Speaker’s going to moderate surliness

blocks.note: the person speaking would say I'll, short for I will; the apostrophe is ignored
to temper something is to moderate or soften it

explanation.surface: The Commons Speaker announces an intention to calm down some rude behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Speaker' suggests the Commons chair or a homophone, but it just means whoever is talking, who says I'll.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad mood or grumpy irritable disposition is surliness, sullen bad humour shown towards others.

clue.text: Daughter and German man stand by sink after washing

blocks.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
Rainer is a common German first name

explanation.surface: A daughter and a German man stand beside the sink once the dishes are washed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand' looks like the verb the daughter and man perform, but it is a noun: a rack.
explanation.definitionFit: A rack placed next to the kitchen basin holds plates and cups while water drips off them.

clue.text: Conceptual artist put tea in ditch

indicators.note: putting one thing in another places it inside, here the drink goes inside the word for ditch

blocks.note: to dump something is to ditch it
cha is an informal word for tea

explanation.surface: An avant-garde artist pours a cup of tea into a trench, perhaps as an installation.
explanation.walkthrough: Marcel Duchamp exhibited a urinal as art, so putting tea in a ditch is just his sort of gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcel Duchamp was the French artist whose readymades founded the idea that art lies in the idea rather than craft.

clue.text: Primarily kale and peppers, suitable for stuffing

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so each of the next three words gives only its opening letter

blocks.note: first letter of kale
first letter of and
first letter of peppers
OK means acceptable, suitable

explanation.surface: A cookery tip: kale and peppers make a good stuffing.
explanation.walkthrough: The vegetable picture suggests stuffing a pepper, but the stuffing is for cushions.
explanation.definitionFit: Kapok is the silky fibre from a tropical tree, used to fill cushions, pillows and life jackets.

clue.text: Family with arms factories runs under a thousand to increase power

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting one piece under another means it comes after it in the grid

blocks.note: K stands for a thousand, as in kilo
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
to up something is to increase it
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: An industrial dynasty whose arms works keep expanding to boost their strength.
explanation.definitionFit: The Krupps of Essen were the German steel dynasty whose works supplied artillery and weapons through two world wars.

clue.text: Rapid turnaround on a point?

blocks.note: surface reading: a quick reversal of a decision or a fast job done to a deadline
setter's reading: a fast spin done on the tip of the toe, as a ballet dancer does

explanation.walkthrough: 'Turnaround' sounds like business jargon for a quick reversal; read literally, it is a spin, and 'on a point' is a dancer on pointe.
explanation.definitionFit: In ballet the dancer whirls a full circle balanced on the tip of one foot, a literal quick spin.

clue.text: Organ tonality includes one reed’s lowest note

indicators.note: what includes something holds it inside, so the word for tonality wraps around the other pieces
in a down entry the lowest letter of a word is its last one

blocks.note: a piece's key is its tonality
I is the Roman numeral one
the bottom letter of reed
N is the abbreviation for note

explanation.surface: A musical remark about a church organ whose pipes include a reed sounding its lowest note.
explanation.walkthrough: The music suggests a pipe organ, but the organ is a body part. The inner letters go in after the K.
explanation.definitionFit: The kidneys are a pair of bodily organs that filter waste from the blood.

clue.text: Organisation of space and length of entry to air passage

blocks.note: NASA is the US space agency
L is the abbreviation for length

explanation.surface: A space agency, and how far it is to get into an air duct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organisation' could suggest an anagram, but it names an actual body.
explanation.definitionFit: The nose is where breath goes into the respiratory tract, and nasal describes anything relating to it.

clue.text: Rigged tally to exclude new socialist

indicators.note: to exclude is to leave out, so the letter for new is taken away from the tally word

blocks.note: an account is a tally or reckoning
N is the abbreviation for new
a red is a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: A fixed vote count was arranged to keep out a new left-wing candidate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rigged' reads as fraudulent, but here it means fitted out, as a ship is rigged.
explanation.definitionFit: Accoutred means dressed or fitted out with equipment, which is what rigged out also means.

clue.text: Jack with years surrounded by sea using inventive language?

indicators.note: what is surrounded sits inside another word, so the years letter goes within the sea word

blocks.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in cards
an ocean is a sea
Y is the abbreviation for years

explanation.surface: An old sailor, a jack tar, spends years at sea and develops a colourful turn of phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: James Joyce, author of Ulysses and Finnegans Wake, famously coined words and bent language, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in the manner of James Joyce plays freely with words, coining new ones and twisting syntax.

clue.text: A drug conveyer with petty officer in a small vessel

indicators.note: the officer's letters are placed in the middle of the drug carrier word

blocks.note: taken as written
a mule is someone who smuggles drugs
PO is the abbreviation for petty officer

explanation.surface: A drug smuggler and a naval officer travel in a little boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a boat to fit the sailor, but it is a sealed glass phial; the officer goes inside the smuggler, not the A.
explanation.definitionFit: An ampoule is a tiny sealed glass container holding a single dose of liquid medicine.

clue.text: To nick spy chief follows decorum

blocks.note: M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories
behaving with decorum, someone is appropriate

explanation.surface: A spymaster stealing something while keeping up appearances.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads as a sentence: M is appropriate, meaning the spy chief behaves properly. Nick is British slang for steal.
explanation.definitionFit: To nick is British slang for steal, and to misappropriate is to take funds or property dishonestly for oneself.

clue.text: Reports of Triad possibly sound, when heads make switch a concealed weapon

indicators.note: reports are things heard, so what matters is the sound of the words rather than their spelling
the starting sounds of the two words change places, the swap named after Reverend Spooner

blocks.note: a triad is a chord of three notes, which sounds like cord; its opening sound is swapped
sound as in of sound mind, sane; its opening sound is swapped

explanation.surface: Accounts that a Chinese criminal gang is in good shape, until the leaders swap and someone hides a blade.
explanation.walkthrough: Triad suggests the Chinese gang, but it is a three-note chord. Swapping the K and S sounds of cord sane gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sword cane is a walking stick with a blade hidden inside its hollow shaft, so the weapon is disguised.

clue.text: Queen tussling with a Lib, not fairly matched?

indicators.note: tussling means wrestling and struggling, so these letters are thrown about into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written; Lib is short for a Liberal

explanation.surface: The monarch wrestles a Liberal politician in a contest that is hardly even.
explanation.definitionFit: Inequable means uneven or unequal, which suits two sides in a struggle that are badly mismatched in strength.

clue.text: Pinch toy after rocking to induce sleep

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective, meaning tending to induce sleep

indicators.note: rocking shakes things back and forth, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

blocks.note: the two words taken as written

explanation.surface: A baby squeezes a toy after being rocked, to send them off to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypnotic describes something that brings on drowsiness or a trance, like a soporific drug or a lulling rhythm.

clue.text: Sign by this motorway’s last for us, seeing that bank

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter only

blocks.note: the final letter of motorway
something for us is ours
since means seeing that, because
to bank on something is to rely on it

explanation.surface: A road sign at the end of the motorway marks our turning near a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign' looks like a road sign, but it is signing a letter with this closing phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The formula is the conventional sign-off written just above the signature at the end of a formal letter.

clue.text: Suffering regular losses, use plan to upload flexible tool

indicators.note: losing letters at regular intervals means every other one drops out

blocks.note: the even letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A business suffering steady losses tries to upload its plan, perhaps with a flexible approach.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like corporate jargon, but the tool is the kitchen kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A spatula is a broad thin bendable blade used in kitchens for spreading, scraping or lifting food.

clue.text: Northern levelling up? It’s in the early stages

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for northern
going up a level is an ascent; the question mark flags the loose sense

explanation.surface: A political slogan: levelling up the north of England is still only just beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: Levelling up was a UK government slogan about investing in northern England, which is what the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent describes something just coming into being, only beginning to develop and not yet mature.

clue.text: General science with a transcendental ring

blocks.note: SCI is a short form of science
pi is a transcendental number in mathematics
the letter O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: General science paired with some mystical, transcendental ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like an adjective for science, but it is the military rank. A transcendental number is one that is not the root of any polynomial.
explanation.definitionFit: Scipio Africanus was the Roman military commander who defeated Hannibal at Zama.

clue.text: All Blacks maybe blocking bad guy before each player’s chance to shine

indicators.note: something blocking a passage sits in the middle of it, so the team letters go inside the following pieces

blocks.note: a cad is a dishonourable man
EA is the abbreviation for each
the All Blacks are the New Zealand rugby team, so NZ

explanation.surface: A rugby team stops a villain before every player gets a chance to show off.
explanation.walkthrough: The team letters go between the E and A of each, after the cad. 'Player' sounds like rugby but means a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadenza is a virtuoso solo passage in a concerto where the soloist shows off skill alone.

clue.text: Not in any way missing wife’s interference

indicators.note: something missing is absent, so the letter for wife is dropped from the first phrase

blocks.note: nowise is an old word meaning not at all
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A husband insists he is not at all bothered by his wife's absence or her meddling.
explanation.definitionFit: Noise is unwanted signal disturbance on a line or broadcast, which engineers also call interference.

clue.text: Tiny amount of broth — a swiz

blocks.note: broth is a thin soup
a swiz is British slang for a swindle, a con

explanation.surface: A diner complains that the meagre bowl of broth is a rip-off.
explanation.walkthrough: A swiz is British slang for a cheat or disappointment.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed from French, the word means a mere trace or hint, a very small quantity of a flavour.

clue.text: Crack and Charlie given up

blocks.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
something given up has been left behind

explanation.surface: Someone has given up crack cocaine, and Charlie, which is slang for cocaine, too.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleft is a split or fissure, a narrow opening in rock or ground, that is, a fissure.

clue.text: Nothing original in parking angle to north or south

blocks.note: P is the sign for parking
latitude is the angular distance north or south of the equator

explanation.surface: There is nothing new about parking at an angle facing north or south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing original' looks like a comment on the parking but is the definition, a trite remark.
explanation.definitionFit: A platitude is a stale overused remark, a cliché with no originality or freshness to it.

clue.text: Time for conclusion of hopeless complaint

indicators.note: one thing in place of another: the time letter replaces the end of the following word

blocks.note: a bleak outlook is hopeless
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: It is time to end a pointless grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: To bleat is to whine or moan feebly, so a bleat is a weak, plaintive grumble.

clue.text: Bedder’s somewhat pricey — exorbitant in retrospect

indicators.note: somewhat means part of, so only some letters inside the words are taken
retrospect looks backwards, so the letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: letters running across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A Cambridge college cleaner, a bedder, is pricey, even outrageously so, looking back.
explanation.walkthrough: At Cambridge a bedder is a college cleaner, which the surface uses; here it means a bedding plant, and the oxeye is a daisy.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardeners call plants set out in flower beds bedders, and the oxeye daisy is grown that way.

clue.text: Genuine article, the makings of echt unit

indicators.note: makings are raw materials, so the following words' letters are used to build something new

blocks.note: A is the indefinite article
the two words taken as written supply the letters

explanation.surface: A real article, made from something truly echt, the German for genuine.
explanation.walkthrough: Echt is borrowed from German and means real, so the surface is a self-referential joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Authentic means real and not fake, exactly what echt and genuine both mean.
